title.en: Genetic engineering, stem cells and DNA fingerprinting

text.en: In 1996 Dolly, a cloned sheep, was born at the Roslin Institute. Her story opens the world of genetic engineering and biotechnology.

Genetic engineering is the manipulation and transfer of genes from one organism to another, creating recombinant DNA (rDNA).
Tools: plasmid vectors, restriction enzymes that cut DNA at specific sites, and DNA ligases that join the fragments.
Gene cloning steps: isolate the desired gene, insert into a plasmid vector, transfer into a bacterium, select and multiply, and express the gene.
Dolly was the first cloned female sheep, developed by Ian Wilmut at Roslin Institute, Scotland in 1996 by somatic cell nuclear transfer; she lived 6.5 years.
Medicine: insulin (first commercial rDNA product by Eli Lilly, 1979), human growth hormone, clotting factors, tissue plasminogen activator and vaccines.
Gene therapy replaces a defective gene with a functional one; it is somatic or germ line, and was first implemented in 1990.
Stem cells are undifferentiated cells that self-renew and differentiate; they may be embryonic or adult stem cells and are used in stem cell therapy.
DNA fingerprinting, developed by Alec Jeffreys, uses VNTRs in satellite DNA to identify individuals, in forensics and paternity tests.
Genetically modified organisms: Golden rice carries a beta-carotene gene and Bt crops carry a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis that kills insects.

problem.en: Explain how DNA fingerprinting can identify a criminal.

text.en: 99 percent of human DNA is the same, but 1 percent differs as satellite DNA with VNTRs.
DNA from the crime scene is compared with a suspect's by band patterns.
Only identical twins share the same pattern.

prompt.en: State two differences between somatic and germ line gene therapy.

requiredIdeas.en: Somatic: body cells, not passed to the next generation
Germ line: egg and sperm cells, passed on
Only somatic therapy has been done till date

points.en: rDNA technology uses enzymes and plasmids.
Insulin was the first rDNA drug.
Golden rice and Bt crops are GM plants.
